findings.issue: References [1] and [2] are bibliographically identical — both cite Herman JP et al., Compr Physiol 2016;6(2):603–621, PMID 27065163, DOI 10.1002/cphy.c150015. The same paper appears under two separate reference numbers, covering synthesis/StAR ([1]) and HPA cascade/AVP/negative-feedback/CNS effects ([2]). This is structural redundancy, not fabrication — both PMIDs are real and verified — but it inflates the apparent citation count and could mislead a reader into expecting two distinct sources.
findings.recommended_fix: Collapse [1] and [2] into a single reference number (e.g., [1]) and update all inline citations to use that single number. The paper legitimately supports all claims currently attributed to both entries.

summary: Section A covers HPA-axis physiology thoroughly and accurately: all seven bibliography entries are real, peer-reviewed tier-1 mechanism reviews; two PMIDs spot-checked (27065163 and 39177247) fully confirmed; all unit conversions (µg/dL ↔ nmol/L ×27.6) verified correct; all inline citations carry type tags; mechanistic chain and CBG/11β-HSD physiology are accurate. One WARN: references [1] and [2] point to the same paper (Herman et al. 2016, PMID 27065163) — a redundant listing that depresses citation_fidelity to 90 but does not breach the 92 total threshold.
